column1: # THE RENDERER -- aontu render (docs/design/RENDER.0.md; RENDER P3, the
# fragment fold). A document is evaluated, the value at `ask.at` (the
# root by default) is vetted against the bundled aontu:code vocabulary,
# and code.units is folded into bytes: one string per unit, the loss
# Columns: name<TAB>render<TAB>src<TAB>{"ask": {at?, profiles?, unit?, strict?}, "verdict", "units", "lossy"} -- or "errors" on error
# The options ride `expect.ask` as view's do: the same document renders
# differently under a caller-supplied profile, a unit filter, or strict.
# Newlines in a unit's text are written \n, which the runner's escape
# pass expands. Every expectation was obtained by running BOTH engines
# THE FOLD (D2, D3, D6). A bare string piece is a line at depth 0; a
# line is pad(at) + text + LF, and an empty text emits no pad; a blank
# is its terminators alone; a raw block's lines each get the pad unless
# reindent is false; nothing is trimmed. The unit is fragment-only, so
# it renders under aontu:lang/text, whose indent is two spaces.
